This architecture will be implemented later by a seeded local code model and evaluated automatically. Produce concrete design and implementation tasks for every file; do not use placeholders.

Normative evaluator protocol (these paths are mandatory and override preferences):
- build file: CMakeLists.txt
- runtime entry: src/Main.cpp
- single test target: tests/test_main.cpp
- test command: ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure
- keep exactly one protocol-level test file; additional non-test implementation files are allowed

Language/layout constraints:
Use include/*.h and src/*.cpp pairs for reusable modules. tests/test_main.cpp must include headers, never implementation .cpp files. Use only the C++17 standard library and CMake; do not fetch dependencies. Every header must be self-contained and list every standard-library include needed by its declarations; every source must include algorithms/types it uses.

Medium-size reference from MetaProjectDev (descriptive only; the architecture model's generated file count is authoritative):
- about 8 repository files
- about 35 functions or methods
- about 700 lines of code

Sizing guidance:
- #Files, #Functions, and #LOC above are paper-table references, not acceptance bounds
- use the number of files produced by this architecture run; do not add or remove files merely to hit the reference
- count build, runtime, test, package markers, headers, and implementation files when reporting the realized size

Required domain behavior:
- bird position and flap physics
- gravity and deterministic ticks
- pipe movement and gaps
- collision rules
- score updates when pipes pass
- game-over and reset

Cross-cutting requirements:
- separate pure domain logic from runtime, UI, filesystem, network, clock, and randomness boundaries
- automated tests must be deterministic, headless, offline, and require no manual interaction
- keep the single test target concise (2 to 4 tests, preferably under 150 LOC): cover runtime wiring and representative core rules, not the full feature matrix
- do not inflate the function/LOC target with test code; put substantive behavior in implementation files
- make every planned file small enough for one 4096-token code completion: prefer under 150 LOC and never plan a file over 220 LOC
- order the Task list strictly by implementation dependency: foundational types and interfaces first, then dependent implementations, then the runtime entry, and the single test target LAST (the build descriptor may be first)
- the Engineer code_todos must preserve that dependency-first Task-list order so later files can see already-generated dependency code
- the runtime entry must provide a small non-interactive demonstration that exits successfully or starts safely without an output loop
- validate invalid inputs and boundary cases
- keep public interfaces coherent across design, task list, implementation, and tests
- specify one canonical public API; tests must use it without inventing alternate semantics
- make Full API spec non-empty and exhaustive: for every public type/function give its exact module, signature, return value, error behavior, and key semantics; repeat these exact contracts in each affected file task
- tests may import only the canonical public API and should assert stable externally visible behavior, not private implementation details, incidental formatting, or unplanned aliases
- avoid circular dependencies; explicitly give the allowed import/include direction and ensure every referenced symbol is defined before a dependent file is generated
- avoid network access and OS-specific behavior during build, tests, and runtime checks
- all planned source, header, build, and test files must be listed exactly and consistently in the design and task documents

Generate a complete medium-size C++17 repository architecture for: Flappy bird game.

This architecture will be implemented later by a seeded local code model and evaluated automatically. Produce concrete design and implementation tasks for every file; do not use placeholders.

Normative evaluator protocol (these paths are mandatory and override preferences):
- build file: CMakeLists.txt
- runtime entry: src/Main.cpp
- single test target: tests/test_main.cpp
- test command: ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure
- keep exactly one protocol-level test file; additional non-test implementation files are allowed

Language/layout constraints:
Use include/*.h and src/*.cpp pairs for reusable modules. tests/test_main.cpp must include headers, never implementation .cpp files. Use only the C++17 standard library and CMake; do not fetch dependencies. Every header must be self-contained and list every standard-library include needed by its declarations; every source must include algorithms/types it uses.

Medium-size reference from MetaProjectDev (descriptive only; the architecture model's generated file count is authoritative):
- about 8 repository files
- about 35 functions or methods
- about 700 lines of code

Sizing guidance:
- #Files, #Functions, and #LOC above are paper-table references, not acceptance bounds
- use the number of files produced by this architecture run; do not add or remove files merely to hit the reference
- count build, runtime, test, package markers, headers, and implementation files when reporting the realized size

Required domain behavior:
- bird position and flap physics
- gravity and deterministic ticks
- pipe movement and gaps
- collision rules
- score updates when pipes pass
- game-over and reset

Cross-cutting requirements:
- separate pure domain logic from runtime, UI, filesystem, network, clock, and randomness boundaries
- automated tests must be deterministic, headless, offline, and require no manual interaction
- keep the single test target concise (2 to 4 tests, preferably under 150 LOC): cover runtime wiring and representative core rules, not the full feature matrix
- do not inflate the function/LOC target with test code; put substantive behavior in implementation files
- make every planned file small enough for one 4096-token code completion: prefer under 150 LOC and never plan a file over 220 LOC
- order the Task list strictly by implementation dependency: foundational types and interfaces first, then dependent implementations, then the runtime entry, and the single test target LAST (the build descriptor may be first)
- the Engineer code_todos must preserve that dependency-first Task-list order so later files can see already-generated dependency code
- the runtime entry must provide a small non-interactive demonstration that exits successfully or starts safely without an output loop
- validate invalid inputs and boundary cases
- keep public interfaces coherent across design, task list, implementation, and tests
- specify one canonical public API; tests must use it without inventing alternate semantics
- make Full API spec non-empty and exhaustive: for every public type/function give its exact module, signature, return value, error behavior, and key semantics; repeat these exact contracts in each affected file task
- tests may import only the canonical public API and should assert stable externally visible behavior, not private implementation details, incidental formatting, or unplanned aliases
- avoid circular dependencies; explicitly give the allowed import/include direction and ensure every referenced symbol is defined before a dependent file is generated
- avoid network access and OS-specific behavior during build, tests, and runtime checks
- all planned source, header, build, and test files must be listed exactly and consistently in the design and task documents

- struct IRandom { virtual ~IRandom() noexcept = default; virtual double nextUnit() = 0; }.
- class LcgRandom : public IRandom { explicit LcgRandom(std::uint64_t seed); std::uint64_t nextUint64(); double nextUnit() override; }.
Semantics: LcgRandom implements a 64-bit LCG with constants a=6364136223846793005, c=1; state is updated per call. nextUint64() returns the new state; nextUnit() returns (nextUint64() / (std::numeric_limits<uint64_t>::max()+1.0)) in [0,1).

include/GameConfig.h: struct GameConfig {
 double worldWidth, worldHeight; double gravity; double flapImpulse; double maxFallSpeed; double pipeSpeed; double pipeWidth; double pipeGapHeight; double pipeSpawnInterval; double birdX; double birdWidth; double birdHeight;
 static GameConfig Default(); void validate() const; }.
Semantics: Default() returns sane gameplay values. validate() throws std::invalid_argument on invalid: non-positive sizes/speeds; pipeGapHeight < worldHeight must hold; 0 <= birdX <= worldWidth-birdWidth; pipeWidth > 0; pipeSpawnInterval > 0; etc.

include/Bird.h: class Bird { public: Bird(double y0, double v0); void flap(const GameConfig& cfg); void update(double dt, const GameConfig& cfg); double y() const noexcept; double velocity() const noexcept; double top(const GameConfig& cfg) const noexcept; double bottom(const GameConfig& cfg) const noexcept; void reset(double y0) noexcept; }.
Semantics: Coordinates: y increases upward; top() = y()+birdHeight/2; bottom() = y()-birdHeight/2. flap() adds positive cfg.flapImpulse to velocity. update() applies gravity (v -= cfg.gravity*dt), clamps v >= -cfg.maxFallSpeed, integrates y += v*dt, clamps bird within [0, worldHeight] using std::clamp; touching top or bottom clamps position and may be considered a boundary contact by GameState.

include/Pipe.h: class Pipe { public: double x; double gapY; bool scored; Pipe(double x0, double gapY0); void update(double dt, const GameConfig& cfg); bool isOffscreen(const GameConfig& cfg) const; bool hasPassedBird(double birdX, const GameConfig& cfg) const; bool collidesWithBird(double birdX, double birdTop, double birdBottom, const GameConfig& cfg) const; }.
Semantics: Pipes move left at cfg.pipeSpeed: x -= cfg.pipeSpeed * dt. isOffscreen() true when x + pipeWidth < 0. hasPassedBird() true when x + pipeWidth < birdX. collidesWithBird() performs axis-aligned check: if bird overlaps pipe x-range [x, x+pipeWidth], then collision occurs unless bird is within vertical gap [gapY - pipeGapHeight/2, gapY + pipeGapHeight/2].

include/GameState.h: class GameState { public: explicit GameState(GameConfig cfg); void reset(); void flap(); void update(double dt, IRandom& rng); int score() const noexcept; bool gameOver() const noexcept; const std::vector<Pipe>& pipes() const noexcept; double birdY() const noexcept; double birdTop() const noexcept; double birdBottom() const noexcept; }.
Semantics: Owns Bird, Pipes, score, gameOver flag, and a spawn timer. Constructor stores cfg and initializes Bird centered vertically with zero velocity. reset() clears pipes/score/timer and recenters Bird. flap() delegates to Bird unless gameOver. update(): if gameOver, returns; else updates Bird, updates existing Pipes, spawns a new Pipe when timer exceeds cfg.pipeSpawnInterval: gapY derived from rng.nextUnit()*playable-range; clamps gap within play area; increments score exactly once per Pipe when it passes birdX; sets gameOver if collision with a Pipe or if Bird touches top/bottom; removes offscreen Pipes.

include/GameEngine.h: class GameEngine { public: GameEngine(GameConfig cfg, std::unique_ptr<IRandom> rng); void reset(); void flap(); void step(double dt); int score() const noexcept; bool isGameOver() const noexcept; double birdY() const noexcept; const std::vector<Pipe>& pipes() const noexcept; const GameConfig& config() const noexcept; }.
Semantics: Validates cfg in ctor (cfg.validate()). Holds RNG and GameState. step(dt) calls state_.update(dt, *rng_). flap() calls state_.flap() if not game over. reset() reinitializes GameState with same cfg and preserved RNG object/state.

Semantics: Coordinates: y increases upward; top() = y()+birdHeight/2; bottom() = y()-birdHeight/2. flap() adds positive cfg.flapImpulse to velocity. update() applies gravity (v -= cfg.gravity*dt), clamps v >= -cfg.maxFallSpeed, integrates y += v*dt, clamps bird within [0, worldHeight] using std::clamp; touching top or bottom clamps position and may be considered a boundary contact by GameState.

top() = y()+birdHeight/2; bottom() = y()-birdHeight/2. flap() adds positive cfg.flapImpulse to velocity. update() applies gravity (v -= cfg.gravity*dt), clamps v >= -cfg.maxFallSpeed, integrates y += v*dt, clamps bird within [0, worldHeight] using std::clamp; - struct IRandom { virtual ~IRandom() noexcept = default; virtual double nextUnit() = 0; }.
- class LcgRandom : public IRandom { explicit LcgRandom(std::uint64_t seed); std::uint64_t nextUint64(); double nextUnit() override; }.
Semantics: LcgRandom implements a 64-bit LCG with constants a=6364136223846793005, c=1; state is updated per call. nextUint64() returns the new state; nextUnit() returns (nextUint64() / (std::numeric_limits<uint64_t>::max()+1.0)) in [0,1).

include/GameConfig.h: struct GameConfig {
 double worldWidth, worldHeight; double gravity; double flapImpulse; double maxFallSpeed; double pipeSpeed; double pipeWidth; double pipeGapHeight; double pipeSpawnInterval; double birdX; double birdWidth; double birdHeight;
 static GameConfig Default(); void validate() const; }.
Semantics: Default() returns sane gameplay values. validate() throws std::invalid_argument on invalid: non-positive sizes/speeds; pipeGapHeight < worldHeight must hold; 0 <= birdX <= worldWidth-birdWidth; pipeWidth > 0; pipeSpawnInterval > 0; etc.

include/Bird.h: class Bird { public: Bird(double y0, double v0); void flap(const GameConfig& cfg); void update(double dt, const GameConfig& cfg); double y() const noexcept; double velocity() const noexcept; double top(const GameConfig& cfg) const noexcept; double bottom(const GameConfig& cfg) const noexcept; void reset(double y0) noexcept; }.
Semantics: Coordinates: y increases upward; top() = y()+birdHeight/2; bottom() = y()-birdHeight/2. flap() adds positive cfg.flapImpulse to velocity. update() applies gravity (v -= cfg.gravity*dt), clamps v >= -cfg.maxFallSpeed, integrates y += v*dt, clamps bird within [0, worldHeight] using std::clamp; touching top or bottom clamps position and may be considered a boundary contact by GameState.

include/Pipe.h: class Pipe { public: double x; double gapY; bool scored; Pipe(double x0, double gapY0); void update(double dt, const GameConfig& cfg); bool isOffscreen(const GameConfig& cfg) const; bool hasPassedBird(double birdX, const GameConfig& cfg) const; bool collidesWithBird(double birdX, double birdTop, double birdBottom, const GameConfig& cfg) const; }.
Semantics: Pipes move left at cfg.pipeSpeed: x -= cfg.pipeSpeed * dt. isOffscreen() true when x + pipeWidth < 0. hasPassedBird() true when x + pipeWidth < birdX. collidesWithBird() performs axis-aligned check: if bird overlaps pipe x-range [x, x+pipeWidth], then collision occurs unless bird is within vertical gap [gapY - pipeGapHeight/2, gapY + pipeGapHeight/2].

include/GameState.h: class GameState { public: explicit GameState(GameConfig cfg); void reset(); void flap(); void update(double dt, IRandom& rng); int score() const noexcept; bool gameOver() const noexcept; const std::vector<Pipe>& pipes() const noexcept; double birdY() const noexcept; double birdTop() const noexcept; double birdBottom() const noexcept; }.
Semantics: Owns Bird, Pipes, score, gameOver flag, and a spawn timer. Constructor stores cfg and initializes Bird centered vertically with zero velocity. reset() clears pipes/score/timer and recenters Bird. flap() delegates to Bird unless gameOver. update(): if gameOver, returns; else updates Bird, updates existing Pipes, spawns a new Pipe when timer exceeds cfg.pipeSpawnInterval: gapY derived from rng.nextUnit()*playable-range; clamps gap within play area; increments score exactly once per Pipe when it passes birdX; sets gameOver if collision with a Pipe or if Bird touches top/bottom; removes offscreen Pipes.

include/GameEngine.h: class GameEngine { public: GameEngine(GameConfig cfg, std::unique_ptr<IRandom> rng); void reset(); void flap(); void step(double dt); int score() const noexcept; bool isGameOver() const noexcept; double birdY() const noexcept; const std::vector<Pipe>& pipes() const noexcept; const GameConfig& config() const noexcept; }.
Semantics: Validates cfg in ctor (cfg.validate()). Holds RNG and GameState. step(dt) calls state_.update(dt, *rng_). flap() calls state_.flap() if not game over. reset() reinitializes GameState with same cfg and preserved RNG object/state.

- pipe movement and gaps
- collision rules

- make Full API spec non-empty and exhaustive: for every public type/function give its exact module, signature, return value, error behavior, and key semantics; repeat these exact contracts in each affected file task

- avoid network access and OS-specific behavior during build, tests, and runtime checks
- all planned source, header, build, and test files must be listed exactly and consistently in the design and task documents

Generate a complete medium-size C++17 repository architecture for: Flappy bird game.

This architecture will be implemented later by a seeded local code model and evaluated automatically. Produce concrete design and implementation tasks for every file; do not use placeholders.

Normative evaluator protocol (these paths are mandatory and override preferences):
- build file: CMakeLists.txt
- runtime entry: src/Main.cpp
- single test target: tests/test_main.cpp
- test command: ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure
- keep exactly one protocol-level test file; additional non-test implementation files are allowed

Language/layout constraints:
Use include/*.h and src/*.cpp pairs for reusable modules. tests/test_main.cpp must include headers, never implementation .cpp files. Use only the C++17 standard library and CMake; do not fetch dependencies. Every header must be self-contained and list every standard-library include needed by its declarations; every source must include algorithms/types it uses.

Medium-size reference from MetaProjectDev (descriptive only; the architecture model's generated file count is authoritative):
- about 8 repository files
- about 35 functions or methods
- about 700 lines of code

Sizing guidance:
- #Files, #Functions, and #LOC above are paper-table references, not acceptance bounds
- use the number of files produced by this architecture run; do not add or remove files merely to hit the reference
- count build, runtime, test, package markers, headers, and implementation files when reporting the realized size

Required domain behavior:
- bird position and flap physics
- gravity and deterministic ticks
- pipe movement and gaps
- collision rules
- score updates when pipes pass
- game-over and reset

Cross-cutting requirements:
- separate pure domain logic from runtime, UI, filesystem, network, clock, and randomness boundaries
- automated tests must be deterministic, headless, offline, and require no manual interaction
- keep the single test target concise (2 to 4 tests, preferably under 150 LOC): cover runtime wiring and representative core rules, not the full feature matrix
- do not inflate the function/LOC target with test code; put substantive behavior in implementation files
- make every planned file small enough for one 4096-token code completion: prefer under 150 LOC and never plan a file over 220 LOC
- order the Task list strictly by implementation dependency: foundational types and interfaces first, then dependent implementations, then the runtime entry, and the single test target LAST (the build descriptor may be first)
- the Engineer code_todos must preserve that dependency-first Task-list order so later files can see already-generated dependency code
- the runtime entry must provide a small non-interactive demonstration that exits successfully or starts safely without an output loop
- validate invalid inputs and boundary cases
- keep public interfaces coherent across design, task list, implementation, and tests
- specify one canonical public API; tests must use it without inventing alternate semantics
- make Full API spec non-empty and exhaustive: for every public type/function give its exact module, signature, return value, error behavior, and key semantics; repeat these exact contracts in each affected file task
- tests may import only the canonical public API and should assert stable externally visible behavior, not private implementation details, incidental formatting, or unplanned aliases
- avoid circular dependencies; explicitly give the allowed import/include direction and ensure every referenced symbol is defined before a dependent file is generated
- avoid network access and OS-specific behavior during build, tests, and runtime checks
- all planned source, header, build, and test files must be listed exactly and consistently in the design and task documents

include/Bird.h: class Bird { public: Bird(double y0, double v0); void flap(const GameConfig& cfg); void update(double dt, const GameConfig& cfg); double y() const noexcept; double velocity() const noexcept; double top(const GameConfig& cfg) const noexcept; double bottom(const GameConfig& cfg) const noexcept; void reset(double y0) noexcept; }.

include/Pipe.h: class Pipe { public: double x; double gapY; bool scored; Pipe(double x0, double gapY0); void update(double dt, const GameConfig& cfg); bool isOffscreen(const GameConfig& cfg) const; bool hasPassedBird(double birdX, const GameConfig& cfg) const; bool collidesWithBird(double birdX, double birdTop, double birdBottom, const GameConfig& cfg) const; }.

This architecture will be implemented later by a seeded local code model and evaluated automatically. Produce concrete design and implementation tasks for every file; do not use placeholders.

Use only the C++17 standard library and CMake; do not fetch dependencies. Every header must be self-contained and list every standard-library include needed by its declarations; every source must include algorithms/types it uses.

- count build, runtime, test, package markers, headers, and implementation files when reporting the realized size

- gravity and deterministic ticks
- pipe movement and gaps
- collision rules

- separate pure domain logic from runtime, UI, filesystem, network, clock, and randomness boundaries
- automated tests must be deterministic, headless, offline, and require no manual interaction
- keep the single test target concise (2 to 4 tests, preferably under 150 LOC): cover runtime wiring and representative core rules, not the full feature matrix

- make every planned file small enough for one 4096-token code completion: prefer under 150 LOC and never plan a file over 220 LOC

    class IRandom {

        +~IRandom()

        +nextUnit() double
        +nextUint64() uint64_t
    }
    IRandom <|.. LcgRandom

        +worldWidth: double
        +worldHeight: double
        +gravity: double
        +flapImpulse: double

        +velocity() double
        +top(cfg: GameConfig) double
        +bottom(cfg: GameConfig) double
        +reset(y0: double) void
    }

        +x: double
        +gapY: double
        +scored: bool
        +Pipe(x0: double, gapY0: double)
        +update(dt: double, cfg: GameConfig) void

        +hasPassedBird(birdX: double, cfg: GameConfig) bool
        +collidesWithBird(birdX: double, birdTop: double, birdBottom: double, cfg: GameConfig) bool
    }

    class GameState {
        -cfg_: GameConfig
        -bird_: Bird
        -pipes_: std::vector<Pipe>
        -score_: int
        -gameOver_: bool
        -timeSinceLastPipe_: double
        +GameState(cfg: GameConfig)
        +reset() void
        +flap() void
        +update(dt: double, rng: IRandom&) void
        +score() int
        +gameOver() bool
        +pipes() const std::vector<Pipe>&
        +birdY() double
        +birdTop() double
        +birdBottom() double
    }

    class GameEngine {
        -cfg_: GameConfig
        -rng_: std::unique_ptr<IRandom>
        -state_: GameState
        +GameEngine(cfg: GameConfig, rng: std::unique_ptr<IRandom>)
        +reset() void
        +flap() void
        +step(dt: double) void
        +score() int
        +isGameOver() bool
        +birdY() double
        +pipes() const std::vector<Pipe>&
        +config() const GameConfig&
    }

    GameState --> Bird
    GameState --> Pipe
    GameState --> GameConfig
    GameState ..> IRandom
    GameEngine --> GameState
    GameEngine --> GameConfig
    GameEngine --> IRandom","Program call flow":"sequenceDiagram

include/GameConfig.h: struct GameConfig {
 double worldWidth, worldHeight; double gravity; double flapImpulse; double maxFallSpeed; double pipeSpeed; double pipeWidth; double pipeGapHeight; double pipeSpawnInterval; double birdX; double birdWidth; double birdHeight;
 static GameConfig Default(); void validate() const; }.
Semantics: Default() returns sane gameplay values. validate() throws std::invalid_argument on invalid: non-positive sizes/speeds; pipeGapHeight < worldHeight must hold; 0 <= birdX <= worldWidth-birdWidth; pipeWidth > 0; pipeSpawnInterval > 0; etc.

include/Bird.h: class Bird { public: Bird(double y0, double v0); void flap(const GameConfig& cfg); void update(double dt, const GameConfig& cfg); double y() const noexcept; double velocity() const noexcept; double top(const GameConfig& cfg) const noexcept; double bottom(const GameConfig& cfg) const noexcept; void reset(double y0) noexcept; }.
Semantics: Coordinates: y increases upward; top() = y()+birdHeight/2; bottom() = y()-birdHeight/2. flap() adds positive cfg.flapImpulse to velocity. update() applies gravity (v -= cfg.gravity*dt), clamps v >= -cfg.maxFallSpeed, integrates y += v*dt, clamps bird within [0, worldHeight] using std::clamp; touching top or bottom clamps position and may be considered a boundary contact by GameState.

include/Pipe.h: class Pipe { public: double x; double gapY; bool scored; Pipe(double x0, double gapY0); void update(double dt, const GameConfig& cfg); bool isOffscreen(const GameConfig& cfg) const; bool hasPassedBird(double birdX, const GameConfig& cfg) const; bool collidesWithBird(double birdX, double birdTop, double birdBottom, const GameConfig& cfg) const; }.
Semantics: Pipes move left at cfg.pipeSpeed: x -= cfg.pipeSpeed * dt. isOffscreen() true when x + pipeWidth < 0. hasPassedBird() true when x + pipeWidth < birdX. collidesWithBird() performs axis-aligned check: if bird overlaps pipe x-range [x, x+pipeWidth], then collision occurs unless bird is within vertical gap [gapY - pipeGapHeight/2, gapY + pipeGapHeight/2].

include/GameState.h: class GameState { public: explicit GameState(GameConfig cfg); void reset(); void flap(); void update(double dt, IRandom& rng); int score() const noexcept; bool gameOver() const noexcept; const std::vector<Pipe>& pipes() const noexcept; double birdY() const noexcept; double birdTop() const noexcept; double birdBottom() const noexcept; }.

Constructor stores cfg and initializes Bird centered vertically with zero velocity. reset() clears pipes/score/timer and recenters Bird. flap() delegates to Bird unless gameOver. update(): if gameOver, returns; else updates Bird, updates existing Pipes, spawns a new Pipe when timer exceeds cfg.pipeSpawnInterval: gapY derived from rng.nextUnit()*playable-range; clamps gap within play area; increments score exactly once per Pipe when it passes birdX; sets gameOver if collision with a Pipe or if Bird touches top/bottom; removes offscreen Pipes.

 double worldWidth, worldHeight; double gravity; double flapImpulse; double maxFallSpeed; double pipeSpeed; double pipeWidth; double pipeGapHeight; double pipeSpawnInterval; double birdX; double birdWidth; double birdHeight;
 static GameConfig Default(); void validate() const; }.
Semantics: Default() returns sane gameplay values. validate() throws std::invalid_argument on invalid: non-positive sizes/speeds; pipeGapHeight < worldHeight must hold; 0 <= birdX <= worldWidth-birdWidth; pipeWidth > 0; pipeSpawnInterval > 0; etc.

Semantics: Coordinates: y increases upward; top() = y()+birdHeight/2; bottom() = y()-birdHeight/2. flap() adds positive cfg.flapImpulse to velocity. update() applies gravity (v -= cfg.gravity*dt), clamps v >= -cfg.maxFallSpeed, integrates y += v*dt, clamps bird within [0, worldHeight] using std::clamp; touching top or bottom clamps position and may be considered a boundary contact by GameState.

include/Pipe.h: class Pipe { public: double x; double gapY; bool scored; Pipe(double x0, double gapY0); void update(double dt, const GameConfig& cfg); bool isOffscreen(const GameConfig& cfg) const; bool hasPassedBird(double birdX, const GameConfig& cfg) const; bool collidesWithBird(double birdX, double birdTop, double birdBottom, const GameConfig& cfg) const; }.
